51610954.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human IDO1 assessed as dissociation rate constant at 0.78 to 25 uM by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - SPR experiments: Surface plasmon resonance experiments were performed with a Biacore T200 instrument. The CM5 sensor chip was activated for 420 s with the mixture (400 mM EDC+100 mM NHS) at a flow rate of 10 μL/min. Dilute hIDO1 and TDO protein to 50 μg/mL in immobilization buffer (10 mM Sodium Acetate, pH 4.0), then injected to sample channel at a flow rate of 10 μL/min, and typically resulted in immobilization levels of 4800 RU for IDO1 and 3600 RU for TDO. The chip was deactivated by 1 M Ethanolamine hydrochloride at a flow rate of 10 μL/min for 420 s. The analyte was diluted to 6 concentrations (25, 12.5, 6.25, 3.125, 1.5625, 0.78 and 0 μM) in the analyte buffer (1% DMSO PBST:1 × PBS, 0.005% Tween20, 1% DMSO, pH 7.4). Binding experiments were performed at 25 °C by using a flow rate of 30 μL/min, with 120 s monitoring of association and 200 s monitoring of dissociation.

original_paragraph.Results - Surface plasmon resonance (SPR: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay was used to further prove the direct interaction between the compound 43b and two enzymes. the human recombinant IDO1 and TDO were immobilized on the sensor chip and different concentrations of the compound 43b were injected over the protein surface at a flow rate of 30 μL/min. Equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) values were calculated from the ratio between the dissociation rate constant kd and the association rate constant ka (KD = kd/ka) by Biacore T200 Evaluation Software.
